synchronization_contract.explicit_non_tolerance_rule: None of these four classes authorizes accepting a behavioural difference. The accepted taxonomy is 1 variance class (CONTINUOUS_CSS_PHASE_VARIANCE), 1 declared transient exact-state class (DECLARED_WAAPI_TRANSIENT_STATE) and 2 synchronization classes (SMOOTH_SCROLL_ARRIVAL_SYNCHRONIZATION, CSS_TRANSITION_SETTLE_SYNCHRONIZATION). Both synchronization classes are harness conditions that must be resolved BEFORE an exact comparison; neither is a tolerance. Only the variance class permits a screenshot-diff allowance, and even then state semantics must match.

items.defect: 9 focusable elements, zero authored :focus and :focus-visible rules; focus is browser default outline:auto only.
Six hover-only affordances (.hero-stage lens, .dossier figure, .node, .flow-card, .btn, .topbar nav a) with no authored touch/press activation path on a coarse pointer.
.n5 / .n6 hidden at <=900px by the source's own media query.
.topbar nav hidden at <=900px, removing all 5 section anchors on mobile.

The source's reduced-motion media query kills CSS animation (computed animation-name:none), but the #pulseBtn pulse is a JavaScript Web Animation never gated on prefers-reduced-motion. One real click raises 2 Animation objects (.heart-core 700ms, .logo-close 900ms) and .heart-core visibly scales none -> 1.23041 -> 1.0398 under reduce.
items.s3_must_not: gate, rewrite or suppress this pulse

items.defect: .logo-close cannot be scrolled to its layout centre because it lies past the document scroll maximum.
scroll-behavior:smooth makes programmatic navigation asynchronous; a consumer assuming scrollTo is synchronous reads stale geometry. This invalidated one S2 capture run.
prefers-reduced-motion does not silence authored CSS animations on pseudo-elements, because the source rule targets `*` and the universal selector does not match ::before / ::after.
items.distinct_from: SRC051_REDUCED_MOTION_DOES_NOT_SILENCE_WAAPI_PULSE (D5), which is a JavaScript Web Animation; D8 is authored CSS on pseudo-elements.
items.s3_must_not: repair, mitigate, normalize or document away; the Source is preserved verbatim.

unresolved_observations.observation: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce at 1440x900@DPR1, document.getAnimations() reported 3 running CSSAnimation objects against .hero-orbit (x2) and .radar on BOTH the ORIGINAL and the SPLIT, while getComputedStyle(...).animationName on the parent element read "none" and element-scoped element.getAnimations() returned [] for those same elements.
unresolved_observations.root_cause: The source authors @keyframes spin on .hero-orbit:before, .hero-orbit:after and .radar:after, but its reduced-motion rule is `* { animation:none!important; scroll-behavior:auto!important }`. The universal selector `*` matches elements, not ::before / ::after pseudo-elements, so those authored pseudo-element animations are never disabled. A parent element reading animation-name:none is therefore consistent with a running animation on its own pseudo-element, which is exactly what S2 could not explain.
unresolved_observations.why_previously_unresolved: S2 could not separate a browser bookkeeping artefact from real residual motion: the parent-scoped queries were empty while the document-scoped query listed animations, and 700ms-separated clips of the orbit and radar regions were not pixel-identical. With the pseudo-element animations identified as the authored source, the apparent inconsistency is explained by query scope rather than by a browser defect.
unresolved_observations.consequence: This is source-native reduced-motion behaviour and a preserved frozen defect (D8), NOT a harness defect and NOT a parity tolerance. It is no longer carried as an open observation.
unresolved_observations.must_not: be used to authorize a source change, a repair, or a parity tolerance. The Source is preserved verbatim; CENTRAL accepted the remaining reduced-motion screenshot differences on this basis.
